title: Map five adjacent job titles that reuse my current skills
how: Paste my resume and 3 tasks I enjoy; ask for 5 adjacent job titles with the overlap in skills, the gap for each, and a one-line reason a hiring manager would accept the move.

title: Score candidate roles in a weighted decision matrix
how: Give Claude 4 to 8 roles and my criteria (pay, growth, location, interest) with weights; ask for a scored table in an Artifact I can re-weight, plus the two closest calls explained.

title: Narrow a long list of interests to three focused targets
how: List every role and industry I might want; ask Claude to cluster them and push back until I have three targets, each with a one-sentence reason I am credible for it.

title: Write a one-paragraph search thesis I can say aloud
how: Give my background, target role and why now; ask for a 60-word thesis (who I help, proof, what I want next) that I can reuse in intros, recruiter calls and the top of my profile.

title: Turn a role guess into a test with real job postings
how: Name the role I am considering; ask Research to pull 15 current postings, list the repeated requirements, and tell me which I already meet, which I can fake-it-until in 3 months, and which block me.

title: Assess how realistic a career change is in six months
how: Share my current role, target role, savings runway and weekly hours; ask for a frank feasibility read with milestones, the biggest risk, and a fallback bridge role if it stalls.

title: Find bridge roles that move me toward a stretch target
how: Give my current title and the stretch role; ask for 3 intermediate roles that are realistic now, what each adds to my record, and how long staying is sensible before the next step.

title: Shortlist industries by hiring tailwinds and my background
how: Ask Research for 5 industries hiring in my region, with sources on demand trend, typical roles for someone with my skills, and entry barriers, ending in a ranked shortlist.

title: Design a weekly search plan sized to my available hours
how: Tell Claude my weekly hours, deadline and energy pattern; ask for a week template splitting time among targeting, networking, applying and prep, favoring conversations over blind applications.

title: Convert an offer goal into weekly funnel targets
how: Give my target start date and rough response rates; ask Claude to back-solve how many applications, conversations and interviews per week I need, and flag what to change if numbers lag.

title: Decide between a few tailored or many quick applications
how: Describe my market, seniority and time; ask Claude for a recommended split such as 20 percent deep tailored and 80 percent light, with the reasoning and when to shift.

title: Weigh staying in my job versus starting a search
how: List what I like and dislike about my job, my financial buffer and market risk; ask Claude for a pros and cons table and three cheap experiments before I commit to leaving.

title: Build a 30-day action plan after a layoff
how: Give my severance end date, benefits deadlines and target roles; ask for a day-by-day first 30 days covering paperwork, outreach to former colleagues, materials refresh and a daily schedule that protects rest.

title: Write a dealbreakers and must-haves list I screen offers with
how: Interview me with 10 questions about pay floor, commute, culture and growth; ask Claude to produce a must-have, nice-to-have and dealbreaker list I can apply to every posting in under a minute.

title: Match company size and stage to my working style
how: Describe how I like to work (structure, pace, ownership); ask Claude which of startup, mid-size, enterprise or public sector fits best, with the trade-offs for pay, stability and learning.

title: Explore public sector and nonprofit paths for my skills
how: Give my skills and region; ask Research to identify agencies, nonprofits and contractors that hire for them, how their application process differs, and typical timelines.

title: Compare freelancing against full-time for my situation
how: Share my skills, expenses and risk tolerance; ask Claude for a comparison with income needed, client acquisition effort and a 60-day test plan for freelancing as a bridge.

title: Plan a search focused on remote-first employers
how: Tell Claude my time zone and role; ask for the types of employers that hire remotely in it, the time-zone and contract constraints to check, and the exact search phrases to use.

title: Plan a search around a move to another city or country
how: Name the candidate cities and role; ask Research to compare job density, pay, cost of living and visa routes, ending in a ranked list with the first 5 actions for the top pick.

title: Plan a job search targeting Latin American employers
how: Give my role and countries of interest; ask Research for employers and boards active there, hiring norms by country, language expectations and pay currency issues, and what differs from a US search.

title: Position bilingual Spanish and English skills as a core advantage
how: Share my roles and language level; ask Claude which role families pay a premium for bilingual ability, how to state proficiency honestly, and a positioning line for each target.

title: Pick the best metro for my occupation
how: Give my occupation and constraints; ask Research for the metros with the most openings and best pay-to-rent ratio for it, citing public data, and return a top five with trade-offs.

title: Draft the one-minute story of why I am changing careers
how: Give my past roles and reason for change; ask for a 60-second story that frames the move as a pull toward the new field with two proof points, plus a shorter 20-second version.

title: Build a strategy for returning to work after a career gap
how: Share the length and reason for my gap and my last role; ask for a plan covering how to explain it, which roles suit a re-entry, returnship programs to look for, and refreshers to complete.

title: Define target companies and board-level roles for a senior search
how: Give my leadership scope and sector; ask Claude for the company profiles (stage, size, mandate) where my track record maps to an open problem, and the search-firm and network routes to reach them.

title: Build a first-job plan for a final-year student
how: Give my major, graduation date, and experience; ask for a semester-by-semester calendar of recruiting deadlines, internships, career-center steps and application targets.

title: Plan an internship search with deadlines and fallback options
how: Give my year, major and target industries; ask Claude for the typical posting and deadline calendar, early-cycle programs, and a fallback list of smaller employers and research roles.

title: Compare graduate school against entering the job market
how: Share my field, debt and target roles; ask for a structured comparison with payback timelines, roles needing the degree, and what working first would let me test.

title: Identify employers likely to sponsor my visa type
how: Name my visa category and role; ask Research to use public sponsorship filing data to list employers who filed for similar roles, with counts, and to flag how reliable each data source is.

title: Build a search timeline around a visa deadline
how: Give my visa end date, grace period rules from official sources I paste, and target roles; ask for a backwards calendar with application, interview and filing milestones.

title: Shortlist roles that hire on skills over a degree
how: Give my skills and proof; ask Research to find roles and employers whose postings drop degree requirements, with examples, and how they assess skill instead.

title: Plan a search for part-time or flexible roles
how: State my hours, pay and schedule limits; ask Claude which roles and employers commonly offer those terms, phrases to search, and a script for asking about flexibility early.

title: Build a tiered list of 40 target employers
how: Give my role, location and values; ask Research for 40 employers in three tiers (dream, probable, safety), with a one-line fit reason and a hiring signal for each, as a table.

title: Create a rubric to score each employer against my priorities
how: Give my top five priorities; ask for an Artifact scoring sheet with weights where I enter facts per employer and it ranks them, with notes on how to verify each fact.

title: Prioritize this week's postings by my odds and upside
how: Paste 15 postings and my resume; ask Claude to rate each on match, competition guess and upside, and name the five worth tailoring for, with reasons.

title: Reality-check whether I am aiming at the right level
how: Paste my resume and three target postings; ask Claude to judge level fit, say where I am over or under, and list the evidence I would need to claim the higher level.

title: Find a niche within my field that reduces competition
how: Share my skills and past projects; ask for 5 narrow niches (sector plus specialty) where my record is unusually strong, and the search terms to find roles in each.

title: Sketch three five-year career paths and their first moves
how: Give my skills and values; ask Claude for three divergent five-year paths with the first job in each and the signal that would tell me to pick it.

title: Have Claude argue against my chosen targets
how: State my three targets and reasons; ask Claude to play a skeptical mentor and list the strongest objections, then tell me which ones are fixable before I apply.

title: Diagnose a search that gets no replies
how: Share counts of applications, replies and interviews plus my resume and two postings; ask Claude to locate the funnel stage failing and propose three changes to test over two weeks.

title: Run the search as small weekly experiments
how: Give last week's funnel numbers; ask Claude to propose one change to test (title phrasing, channel, message), the metric that will tell me it worked, and when to stop.

title: Plan a four-week sprint to close the biggest skill gap
how: Give the gap found in postings and my weekly hours; ask for a four-week plan with one deliverable per week that I can show on a resume or in an interview.

title: Find sectors where my skills pay the most
how: Give my skills and location; ask Research to compare pay for similar roles across sectors using public data and name three sectors worth targeting, with the trade-offs.

title: Plan a search for jobs with travel or long time off
how: State how much travel or leave I want; ask Claude which employers and role types offer it, phrases to search, and how to verify policies before applying.

title: Find roles that give varied, non-repetitive work
how: Describe tasks that bore or energize me; ask Claude to identify role types and employer models (consultancies, small teams, rotations) with variety and the red-flag phrases in postings.

title: Plan an entry route into a regulated field
how: Name the field; ask Research for licenses, certifications and entry roles required, the typical timeline and cost, and which of my existing credentials transfer.

title: Choose the right sales role type for my strengths
how: Describe my past work and temperament; ask Claude to compare roles such as development, account executive and customer-facing technical sales, with quota realities, and recommend one.

title: Map entry routes into consulting from my background
how: Share my background; ask Claude to separate firm types (strategy, boutique, independent), explain how each hires, and name the skills and stories I need to emphasize for each.

title: Map my route into product or project management
how: Give my skills and any related projects; ask for the three most realistic entry roles (associate, coordinator, ops-to-product), what proof they want, and a plan to produce it.

title: Pick between support, success and solutions roles
how: Describe my strengths in problem solving, relationships and technical depth; ask Claude to explain how the three tracks differ in day-to-day work, pay and promotion, and recommend one.

title: Translate operations experience into target roles
how: Paste my operations duties and metrics; ask Claude to list roles in supply chain, program management and analytics where those metrics count, with the title variants to search.

title: Find roles that reward practical AI and automation skill
how: Give a summary of workflows I automated; ask Research to list role types and employers asking for such skill in postings, and the phrasing hiring teams use, ranked by fit.

title: Build a full skills inventory from my work history
how: Paste my resume, old reviews and project notes; ask Claude to extract every skill, tool and domain with a proof example for each, grouped into strong, usable and rusty.

title: Translate my past duties into the target field's vocabulary
how: Give my duties and three target postings; ask for a two-column map from my wording to the target field's wording, flagging claims I should not make.

title: Have Claude interview me to mine achievement stories
how: Ask Claude to question me one role at a time with probing follow-ups until it has 12 specific stories with situation, action, result and a number, then save them as a bank.

title: Surface numbers for achievements I think are unquantifiable
how: Paste vague bullets; ask Claude to ask me questions that reveal scale, frequency, time saved or money (estimates allowed, labeled), then rewrite each with an honest figure.

title: Extract recurring strengths from past performance reviews
how: Paste reviews, praise emails and peer notes with names removed; ask for themes that repeat three or more times, my likely differentiators, and blind spots mentioned.

title: Run a values clarification conversation to rank what matters
how: Ask Claude to walk me through 15 forced-choice trade-offs (pay versus autonomy, etc.), then summarize my ranked values and how each should shape the roles I pursue.

title: Audit which past tasks gave and drained energy
how: List tasks from my last three jobs and mark each as energizing or draining; ask Claude to find the pattern and the role traits to seek and avoid.

title: Compare my skills against a stack of target postings
how: Give my skills list and 10 target postings; ask for a frequency table of requirements, my coverage percentage, and the top three gaps ranked by how often they appear.

title: Get an honest readiness score for a specific posting
how: Paste the posting and my resume; ask Claude for a 1 to 10 fit score, the three strongest matches, three gaps, and a verdict on whether to apply now or prepare first.

title: Prepare a credible weakness answer from a real gap
how: Tell Claude two actual weaknesses and what I have done about them; ask for a 45-second answer that is honest, specific, avoids a disguised strength and ends with progress.

title: Turn soft skills into evidence a recruiter can verify
how: Name five soft skills I claim; ask Claude to help me find one concrete episode per skill with an outcome someone else could confirm, and drop any I cannot support.

title: Interpret my personality or strengths test results for job use
how: Paste results of a strengths or personality test; ask Claude to explain the result cautiously, name tasks it suggests and note the limits of such tests so I do not over-rely on them.

title: Recognize unpaid and informal experience worth listing
how: Describe volunteering, side projects, family business or community roles; ask which belong on a resume, how to phrase them for a target job, and which to leave out.

title: Document leadership evidence without a manager title
how: Describe times I led work informally; ask Claude to frame each as scope, people influenced and result, and suggest wording that signals leadership without overstating my title.

title: Summarize my management scope precisely
how: Give team sizes, budgets, turnover and results; ask Claude for a two-line scope statement and five metrics a hiring committee would value, in order of importance.

title: Grade my technical skills by depth for honest claims
how: List my tools and languages with the longest project for each; ask Claude to grade each as expert, working or familiar so my resume claims match what I can defend in an interview.

title: Inventory the domain knowledge I hold beyond skills
how: Describe regulations, processes and customer types I know deeply; ask Claude to list the domain knowledge as selling points for employers who need people who already know the ground.

title: Reconstruct a clean timeline of jobs and gaps
how: Paste dates, titles, and fragments from old files; ask Claude to build one verified timeline, flag overlaps and gaps, and write a short honest explanation for each gap.

title: Set up a running achievement log I update monthly
how: Create a Project with a template for date, task, result, metric and stakeholder; each week paste notes and ask Claude to file entries and highlight which ones are resume-worthy.

title: State language ability using a recognized scale
how: Describe how I use Spanish at work and school; ask Claude to place me on the common proficiency scale and write the one-line wording for the resume with evidence of use.

title: Turn cross-cultural experience into employer-relevant proof
how: Describe work or life across Latin American and US settings; ask Claude to write three examples showing negotiation, translation of norms or market knowledge, in outcome terms.

title: Find job-relevant skills inside hobbies and side projects
how: List my hobbies and projects; ask Claude which demonstrate transferable skills (organizing, data, writing) and how to describe each in a sentence a recruiter respects.

title: Draft a 30-second self-introduction for networking and interviews
how: Give my background and goal; ask for three versions of a 30-second pitch (casual, formal, written) that include one proof point and end with a clear ask.

title: Build the answer to tell me about yourself in three parts
how: Paste my resume and the target posting; ask for a present-past-future answer of 90 seconds that opens with my strongest relevant fact and ends on why this role.

title: Check which credentials are worth listing and which are noise
how: List all my certificates, courses and awards; ask Claude to rank them by relevance to my targets and recommend which to keep, shorten or remove.

title: Map my current role's hidden overlaps with the target role
how: Give a day-in-the-life of my current job and a target posting; ask Claude to find the 10 overlaps people overlook and suggest evidence I can gather for each.

title: Choose five keywords I want associated with me
how: Give my resume and target roles; ask Claude to pick five keywords that recruiters search and I can prove, and show where each should appear in resume and profile.

title: Inventory who could vouch for me and for what
how: List managers, peers and clients; ask Claude to match each person to the claims they could confirm, flag who needs a refresher on my recent work, and who not to ask.

title: Look for patterns in past rejection feedback
how: Paste rejection emails and any feedback; ask Claude to find patterns, separate fixable issues from fit, and propose two changes to materials or interview answers.

title: Review my resume as a skeptical hiring manager
how: Paste the posting and my resume; ask Claude to role-play a hiring manager with 30 seconds and list what they would doubt, the questions they would ask, and what to cut.

title: Estimate what my skills are worth before I look at offers
how: Give my role, years, location and notable results; ask Claude for a pay range logic that lists the data I must verify, factors that push up, and a number I should not go below.

title: Prepare a failure story that shows learning
how: Describe a real project that went wrong; ask Claude to structure a 2-minute story with ownership, the cost, what I changed and later evidence it worked, without blaming others.

title: Prepare a workplace conflict story that stays professional
how: Describe a disagreement with a colleague; ask for a version that explains both views fairly, my action, the result and what I would do earlier next time.

title: Rank my accomplishments by relevance to a target role
how: Paste my achievement list and a posting; ask Claude to order the top eight by relevance to that role, mark which deserve a resume bullet, and which only an interview story.

title: Review career wins and regrets for guidance on next step
how: Write down five wins and three regrets; ask Claude to draw out what I want more or less of next, and turn the answers into three criteria for the next role.

title: Document evidence that I learn fast in new settings
how: Describe times I learned a new tool, team or industry quickly; ask Claude to write three proof points with time-to-productivity and results to counter concerns about my fit.

title: Frame long experience as current rather than dated
how: Paste my resume and recent learning; ask Claude to suggest what to compress, which recent tools and projects to foreground, and wording that signals current practice.

title: Frame caregiving or a gap year as relevant experience
how: Describe what I did during the break; ask Claude for a factual, confident one-line explanation and any transferable work I can honestly list.

title: List my experience before my first full-time job
how: List coursework, projects, clubs, jobs and volunteering; ask Claude to rank them for a target role and draft bullets with the problem, my action and the result.

title: Translate military experience into civilian job language
how: Paste my service duties, ratings and awards; ask Claude to translate into civilian titles and terms, estimate comparable scope, and suggest target roles that value it.

title: Translate academic work into industry terms
how: Paste my CV, papers and teaching; ask Claude to rewrite into resume language with outcomes for non-academic employers, and name roles that hire researchers.

title: Translate self-employment into a hirable record
how: Describe my business, clients and revenue; ask Claude for resume bullets that show scope, results and teamwork, and talking points that answer why I want to be employed.

title: Find my rare combination of skills and write it down
how: List my skills, industries and languages; ask Claude to find unusual pairings that a few candidates share and write a one-line statement that makes me memorable for a specific role.

title: List what evidence I lack for each target claim
how: Give my top five resume claims; ask Claude to mark each as proven, partly proven or asserted only, and propose a quick way to gain proof for the weakest two.

title: Draft a feedback request to colleagues about my strengths
how: Ask Claude to write a short message to 5 colleagues asking for 2 strengths and 1 growth area with examples, easy to answer in three sentences, then summarize replies I paste.

title: Profile my work habits to match a working style
how: Describe my best and worst work days; ask Claude to infer the structure, meeting load and autonomy I need, and turn it into questions to ask employers.

title: Reframe imposter feelings with evidence from my record
how: Paste my accomplishments and a posting I doubt; ask Claude to show where I meet requirements with evidence and give me three facts to repeat before interviews.

title: Check an opportunity against my stated values
how: Share my ranked values and the opportunity's facts; ask Claude to rate alignment on each, point out what is unknown, and list the questions to resolve before I decide.

title: Audit my repos for the skills they actually show
how: Point Claude Code at my repositories; ask it to list which skills the code evidences, weak spots a reviewer would notice, and the two repos worth polishing first.

title: Score my readiness across interview skills
how: Describe how I have done in past interviews; ask Claude to rate me on storytelling, clarity, research and questions, and give a two-week drill plan for the weakest two.

title: Describe my communication style and how to flex it
how: Give three emails and a meeting summary I wrote; ask Claude to describe my style, its strengths for target roles and where I should adapt for interviewers.

title: Calculate my search runway and the pay I need
how: Give my expenses, savings and severance; ask for an Artifact calculator of runway in months and the minimum monthly pay at which I should accept an offer, with scenarios.

title: Build a pay range for a role from public data
how: Give role, city and years of experience; ask Research for ranges from government wage statistics and posted salaries, show sources, and give a low, mid and high number for me.

title: Extract pay ranges from postings in jurisdictions that require them
how: Ask Research to collect 20 recent postings for my role in places that mandate pay ranges, list the ranges by company size, and flag outliers to calibrate my ask.

title: Compare offers adjusted for cost of living
how: Give two offers with cities, rent and taxes I know; ask Claude to compute a rough after-cost comparison, state assumptions, and say which differences are within error.

title: Get a snapshot of hiring demand for my occupation
how: Ask Research to summarize official employment projections and openings data for my occupation and region, trend direction, and which adjacent occupations are growing faster.

title: Count which skills appear most in postings for my target role
how: Ask Research to sample 25 postings for my role, tally the skills and tools named, and produce a ranked list marking which are must-haves and which merely nice.

title: Map the title variants employers use for one kind of job
how: Give my target role; ask Claude for 15 equivalent and neighboring titles by industry and seniority, plus the title strings that mean something different, so my searches stop missing roles.

title: Learn how an unfamiliar industry makes money in an hour
how: Name the industry; ask Research for a brief on revenue model, key players, roles and typical career ladders, with a glossary of the 20 terms I will hear in interviews.

title: Build a glossary of jargon before networking calls
how: Paste three industry articles and postings; ask for an Artifact glossary of 30 terms with plain definitions and a sample sentence, plus a flashcard mode for review.

title: Identify roles in my field that are shrinking or growing
how: Ask Research to compare employment trend data and AI exposure across roles in my field, and recommend two to move toward and one to avoid with the evidence behind each.

title: Learn when my industry hires most through the year
how: Name my industry; ask Research for hiring seasonality evidence, budget-cycle timing and campus recruiting windows, and build a calendar of when to push hardest.

title: Identify which employers are posting the most roles now
how: Ask Research to find companies in my area with the most new postings for my role over the last month and the reasons visible in news (funding, expansion), ranked by fit.

title: Spot companies likely to hire because of new funding
how: Ask Research to list companies in my sector that announced funding, contracts or expansion in the last 60 days, with the likely teams to grow and the best person to contact.

title: Screen target employers for layoff and stability risk
how: Give a list of employers; ask Research for recent layoff news, financial health indicators, and leadership turnover, summarized as green, amber or red with sources.

title: Map an employer's competitors to talk about the market
how: Name the employer; ask Research for its three nearest competitors, how they differ, and three smart questions or opinions I could raise in an interview about its position.

title: Triangulate what a role actually involves day to day
how: Name a role; ask Research to combine postings, practitioner write-ups and official occupational descriptions into a realistic day, a typical week and the common frustrations.

title: Chart the typical career ladder and timelines for a role
how: Name the role; ask for titles from entry to senior, years typically spent at each level, pay by level and the skills that unlock the next step.

title: Compare certificates by cost, time and hiring value
how: List three certificates I am considering; ask Research to compare cost, hours and whether postings in my field actually ask for them, and recommend one or none.

title: Compare training program outcomes with skepticism
how: Give a program name type and claims; ask Research to find independent outcome data, audit rules and complaints, flag marketing statistics and tell me what to ask the provider.

title: Look up public wage scales and union agreements
how: For public-sector or unionized roles, ask Research to find published pay scales and steps for the employer and explain how grade and step placement work and where negotiation is allowed.

title: Benchmark benefits and time off in my sector
how: Ask Research for typical paid leave, retirement match and health coverage norms in my sector and size band, and which ones are most negotiable.

title: Check how remote my role really is in the market
how: Ask Research for data on remote and hybrid share of postings for my role and region, trends over the past year, and employers that reversed policies.

title: Find sponsorship filing statistics for my occupation
how: Ask Research to pull public filing data for my occupation, list employers with the most approvals, typical wages filed, and warn about data gaps and what the data cannot say.

title: Compare regional markets for the same role
how: Give 4 cities and my role; ask Research for openings, pay and competition indicators from public sources, and give a table with a clear recommendation and caveats.

title: Benchmark salaries for Latin American employers in local and USD terms
how: Name role and country; ask Research for pay ranges in local currency and USD, how remote US employers pay there, and norms such as mandatory bonuses and benefits.

title: Learn local hiring and labor norms for a Latin American country
how: Pick one country; ask Research for contract types, probation, mandated bonuses, notice periods and typical interview practices, flagging what to verify with official local sources.

title: Learn the Spanish job titles and posting terms used locally
how: Give my role and country; ask Claude for the local Spanish titles, phrases for requirements and benefits in postings, and search strings that reach local boards in Spanish.

title: Find US roles that value Spanish and cultural knowledge
how: Ask Research for sectors in the US with heavy Spanish-language need, typical roles and pay premiums, and how postings signal the need so I can search for them.

title: List international employers with a regional hub near me
how: Ask Research for multinationals with regional offices or remote teams covering my country, which functions they hire locally, and where they post.

title: Identify the staffing firms active in my field
how: Name my field and city; ask Research to list recruiting and staffing firms that place my role, how they work, and signs of a reputable one, then rank who to contact first.

title: Check a posting or recruiter against known scam patterns
how: Paste the posting and messages; ask Claude to compare them to common employment-scam patterns (fees, check deposits, chat-only interviews) and say what to verify independently.

title: Assemble a market evidence pack for my pay ask
how: Give the offer and role; ask Research to assemble three data points with sources for the range, adjusted for level and location, in a one-page summary I can cite.

title: Benchmark equity grants for a startup offer
how: Share the grant terms; ask Research for typical equity ranges by stage and level, explain vesting and dilution in plain language, and list questions to ask the company.

title: Model total compensation across offers in a table
how: Give base, bonus, equity, benefits and signing terms; ask for an Artifact calculator for first-year and four-year totals with adjustable assumptions and a note of what is guaranteed.

title: Prepare three current industry trends to discuss
how: Name my industry; ask Research for the three trends with the best evidence in the past year, what each means for the role I want, and a sharp sentence of my view on each.

title: Track regulation changes that affect my target role
how: Ask Research for recent and upcoming rule changes in my regulated field that create hiring demand, which employers are exposed, and phrasing to use in my pitch.

title: Assess how AI changes my occupation and what to learn
how: Ask Research for evidence on how AI is changing tasks in my occupation, which skills are gaining value, and a four-skill learning list I can show within two months.

title: Benchmark freelance rates for bridge work
how: Name my service; ask Research for typical hourly and project rates by experience, how they relate to full-time pay, and a rate card with a floor, standard and rush price.

title: Look up outcomes for my degree and school
how: Ask Research to find official graduate outcome and earnings data for my degree and major, typical first roles, and what the best-placed graduates did differently.

title: Find the employers and employer sizes in my field locally
how: Ask Research how employment in my field splits across large, mid-size and small employers in my metro, and which segment likely hires faster for my seniority.

title: Learn typical time to hire so I pace my search
how: Ask Research for typical time-to-hire in my industry and level, the stages involved, and what delays mean, so I can set expectations for follow-ups and savings.

title: Benchmark my reply rates against realistic norms
how: Give my application and reply counts; ask Research for published norms on callback rates by channel and compare, avoiding a single dubious statistic and noting the range.

title: Learn which tools are trending in my field this year
how: Ask Research which tools and frameworks are growing in postings and community use in my field, with evidence, and pick one I can learn this month.

title: Look up licensing and certification requirements by state
how: Name the occupation and states; ask Research for official licensing board requirements, fees, reciprocity and timelines, citing the board pages and noting what to confirm by phone.

title: Scan employer reputation across review and news sources
how: Name an employer; ask Research to summarize themes from employee reviews, news and regulatory records, separating repeated issues from single complaints, and give questions to ask in interviews.

title: Map rotational and graduate programs hiring now
how: Ask Research for employers with formal early-career programs in my field, deadlines, eligibility and selectivity, formatted as a calendar and a shortlist of eight.

title: Check a nonprofit employer's financial health
how: Paste a nonprofit's name and annual filing text; ask Claude to summarize revenue sources, reserves, program spending share and trends so I know whether the job is stable.

title: Read a public company's filings for hiring signals
how: Give the company; ask Research to read the latest annual report and call transcript for growth priorities, headcount comments and risks, and list talking points tied to my skills.

title: Estimate a startup's runway from public information
how: Give the startup name; ask Research to gather funding rounds, team size, burn clues and customer signals, and estimate whether stability is a concern, with the questions to ask founders.

title: Compare contractor and employee roles in my field
how: Describe my field; ask Claude how contract roles differ in pay, benefits and conversion odds, and when contracting is a strategy to enter a target employer.

title: Scan local and virtual events where my target employers appear
how: Ask Research to find conferences, meetups and panels in the next 60 days attended by employers in my field, and rank them by hiring-manager presence and cost.

title: Build a 10-item reading list to sound current in a new sector
how: Name the sector; ask Research for ten recent, credible articles, reports and podcasts, each with a one-line takeaway I can cite in conversations.

title: Produce a one-page brief on a target employer
how: Give the company name and the posting; ask Research for a one-page brief: what it sells, customers, size, recent news, leadership, competitors and three open problems my role might touch, with sources.

title: Summarize an employer's news from the last 90 days
how: Name the employer; ask Research for dated news, launches, deals and leadership changes from the past 90 days, sorted by relevance to the team I am joining, with links.

title: Profile the likely hiring manager from public material
how: Give the manager's public profile text and talks; ask Claude to summarize career path, stated priorities and vocabulary, then suggest two topics and one question that would resonate in an interview.

title: Prepare for each interviewer using public information
how: Paste interviewer names and public profile text; ask for a table of each person's role, likely concerns and one tailored question, with a warning not to cite anything personal.

title: Infer team structure from postings and public profiles
how: Give three or four postings and public team profile text; ask Claude to infer reporting lines, team size, missing skills and the problem the new hire is meant to solve.

title: Decode what a posting really asks for
how: Paste the posting; ask Claude to rank requirements by importance, translate vague phrases, separate hard requirements from wishes, and list what the employer is worried about.

title: Spot red flags in a job posting before applying
how: Paste the posting; ask Claude to flag vague pay, an excessive stack of duties, churn hints and contradictory requirements, and rate how many to worry about.

title: Read culture signals from an employer's public writing
how: Give the company's careers page, blog and value statements; ask for the culture themes, how they differ from marketing, and interview questions that test whether they are real.

title: Summarize themes in employee reviews with caution
how: Ask Research to read reviews and discussion threads about the employer, report repeated themes by team and period, state sample-size limits, and list questions that probe each concern.

title: Find an employer's time-off and benefits policy
how: Name the employer; ask Research to locate its benefits page, posted leave policies, parental leave, holidays and remote stipends from public sources, and note what must be confirmed in writing.

title: Verify an employer's real remote or hybrid policy
how: Ask Research to compare the posting's remote language with leadership statements, return-to-office news and employee comments, and give questions to ask the recruiter about the policy.

title: Find an employer's posted pay bands and levels
how: Name the employer; ask Research to collect posted ranges from its current postings and public disclosures for my level, and show how bands differ by location and title.

title: Research what an employer's interview process looks like
how: Name the employer and role; ask Research to piece together typical stages, durations, formats and question types from candidate reports and company pages, labeled as unverified, with a prep plan.

title: Collect reported interview questions for a role and employer
how: Ask Research to gather reported questions for the role, remove duplicates, group by type and give me draft answers outlines using my stories, treating reports as unconfirmed.

title: Connect my record to an employer's stated mission
how: Paste the mission and values; ask Claude to match each to a real episode from my record, avoiding flattery, and give a two-sentence answer to why this company.

title: Do a product teardown to impress in interviews
how: Give the product's public pages and my usage notes; ask Claude to structure a teardown with users, jobs-to-be-done, strengths, gaps and three improvement ideas with trade-offs.

title: Learn who the employer's customers are and why they buy
how: Ask Research to find case studies, reviews and pricing that reveal customer segments, buying reasons and pain points, then tie them to my role's likely metrics.

title: Map the leadership team and recent changes
how: Ask Research to list executives, tenures, backgrounds and recent departures from public sources and explain what the pattern suggests about priorities and stability.

title: Understand a startup founder's story and thesis
how: Give founder interviews and posts; ask Claude to summarize the thesis, the pivots, and the tone, and to propose three questions that show I understand the company's bet.

title: Run a quick financial health check on an employer
how: Ask Research for funding, revenue growth, profitability and credit signals from filings or news, summarize risk in plain language, and list what to ask about runway or backlog.

title: Estimate headcount trend from public profile data
how: Give counts of current and former employees by month from public pages; ask Claude to estimate growth or shrinkage, caveats, and which teams appear to be hiring.

title: Infer an employer's tech stack from public clues
how: Give the company's postings, engineering blog and repos; ask Claude to list the likely stack, practices and pain points, and where my experience matches, flagged as inferred.

title: Scan an employer's open-source footprint for conversation topics
how: Point Claude Code at the employer's public repos; ask for what the projects do, activity level, contribution style and a small issue I could understand before the interview.

title: Check an employer's public regulatory and compliance record
how: Ask Research to look up enforcement actions, fines and audit findings in public registries relevant to the sector, and describe how they would affect the team I would join.

title: Draft a note on how an employer is positioned versus rivals
how: Ask Research for three rivals and positioning differences; ask Claude to condense into five bullet points and a view of where my role adds an advantage.

title: Extract takeaways from a public company's earnings call
how: Give the transcript; ask Claude for strategic priorities, repeated words from executives, cost or growth signals and how my skills map, in 10 bullets.

title: Sanity-check an employer's pay against market data
how: Give employer pay data from public pages; ask Research to compare against market ranges for the same role and level and flag where the employer is high, low or unclear.

title: Verify claims about inclusion and flexibility
how: Ask Research to compare the employer's public claims with reported data, benefits and leadership composition, and highlight what is evidenced versus marketing.

title: Check the employer's sponsorship history
how: Name the employer; ask Research to find public filing records for roles and wages sponsored in past years, and compute whether my role and level have precedent, with caveats.

title: Check an employer's presence and hiring in Latin America
how: Ask Research for offices, entities, local hiring and regional strategy, and whether roles are contracted through an employer-of-record, which matters for taxes and benefits.

title: Understand what an employer-of-record arrangement means for me
how: Paste the contract terms; ask Claude to explain who is my legal employer, what benefits and taxes apply, and the questions to ask before accepting, noting it is not legal advice.

title: Build a timeline of an employer's key events
how: Ask Research for dated events (founding, rounds, launches, layoffs, leadership changes) and build an Artifact timeline I can scan in two minutes before an interview.

title: Build a glossary of an employer's internal terms
how: Paste public documentation and posts; ask Claude to list the product names, acronyms and phrases the company uses, with meanings, so I speak their language accurately.

title: Turn research into smart questions for each interview stage
how: Paste my company research notes and interview stage; ask for 8 sharp questions that show preparation, split by recruiter, manager and peers, avoiding anything answerable from the website.

title: Study the career paths of people in my target role
how: Paste public profile text of 8 people in the role; ask Claude to find common backgrounds, entry titles, time in role and skills, and what that says about how they were hired.

title: Analyze which backgrounds a team tends to hire
how: Give public profiles of a team's members; ask Claude to describe common backgrounds and schools, newcomers' prior roles, and which of those I can credibly echo in my pitch.

title: Gauge leadership sentiment responsibly
how: Ask Research for leadership approval trends and the reasons given, weigh them against facts, and say how reliable the sample is before I let it shape my decision.

title: Capture an employer's tone for my application writing
how: Paste the careers page, a recent post and the posting; ask Claude to describe the tone (formal, playful, technical) and give five do and don't wording rules for my cover letter.

title: Read customer reviews to learn the employer's real problems
how: Ask Research to summarize customer reviews of the product, top praise and complaints, and which of my skills address the complaints, with two ideas I could mention in an interview.

title: Check public contracts held by an agency contractor
how: Ask Research to look up public awards and contract notices for the contractor, which agencies and programs they serve, the teams likely to expand, and recompete dates.

title: Check an employer's labor relations record
how: Ask Research for public labor relations filings, strikes or agreements and what they imply for scheduling, pay scales and job security for the role I am considering.

title: Compare what the company says with what people report
how: Give the employer's values page; ask Research to compare each claim to independent evidence, rating consistency as strong, mixed or weak, so I can decide what to probe.

title: Check office location, commute and local conditions
how: Give the office address and my home area; ask Claude for commute options and times to test, building and neighborhood notes to check myself, and questions about hybrid days.

title: Find talks and events where employer staff will appear
how: Ask Research to list upcoming conference talks, webinars and open houses involving the employer, with speakers and topics, and suggest a question I could ask at each.

title: Study how long an employer's postings stay open
how: Give three to five postings with dates; ask Claude to infer how often roles reopen, urgency signals, and whether repeated reposting suggests churn or a ghost listing.

title: Estimate whether a posting is a ghost job
how: Paste the posting, its age and the employer's recent news; ask Claude to rate the likelihood it is stale or a ghost listing and whether a referral attempt is worth the time.

title: Tell whether a posting is direct or from a staffing agency
how: Paste the posting; ask Claude to say whether it looks agency-posted, who the end client might be, and how to ask the recruiter for the client name and pay range professionally.

title: Create a sector company list from public registries
how: Name the sector and region; ask Research to list companies from public registries, industry associations and award lists, tag each by size and hiring signal, and export a table.

title: Find small and mid-size employers that big boards miss
how: Ask Research for 25 small employers in my field and region found through trade bodies, local news and supplier lists, each with a contact route and a reason to approach.

title: Expand my list from competitors and suppliers of a favorite employer
how: Name a company I like; ask Research for its competitors, partners and suppliers that hire for my role, and rank them by size, stage and likelihood to be hiring.

title: Write boolean search strings for job boards
how: Give my target titles, must-have skills and exclusions; ask Claude for five boolean strings for the major boards and search engines, with notes on which syntax each supports.

title: Design saved searches and alerts that catch new postings fast
how: Give my titles, location and must-haves; ask for a set of 8 saved searches and alerts across boards with frequencies, and a naming scheme so I can review them in ten minutes.

title: Build a script that watches company career feeds
how: In a Claude Code repo, ask it to write a script that polls public applicant-tracking feeds for my target companies and keywords, dedupes, and writes new postings to a CSV daily.

title: Watch target career pages for newly added roles
how: Give Claude Code a list of career page URLs; ask for a watcher that diffs each page, ignores noise, and emails or logs only new roles matching my keywords.

title: Turn newsletters and feeds into one daily job digest
how: Ask Cowork to gather job newsletters and feeds each morning, extract new postings that match my criteria, and write a one-page digest with links and fit notes.

title: Triage job-alert emails into a ranked shortlist
how: With the email connector, ask Claude to read this week's job alert emails, drop duplicates and weak fits, and list the top ten by match to my criteria with links.

title: Screen 30 postings against my criteria in one pass
how: Paste 30 postings and my must-haves; ask Claude for a table with fit, deal-breaker flags and a keep, maybe or drop verdict, shortest reason for each.

title: Set a routine to apply within 48 hours of posting
how: Ask Claude to design a morning routine of checking alerts, scoring fit and sending the first application inside 48 hours of posting, with a time budget under 45 minutes.

title: Find leads for roles that are not posted yet
how: Ask Research to find signals of unposted roles (funding, expansions, departures, new offices) for my sector, name the likely hiring manager and suggest the approach for each lead.

title: Map the niche job boards for my field and region
how: Name my field and region; ask Research for specialist boards, association listings and community forums, and rate each on freshness and quality, in a table.

title: Map job boards used in Latin American countries
how: Name my countries and role; ask Research for the boards, regional LinkedIn-style networks and company pages most used there, which languages postings use, and how to filter for remote.

title: Vet remote job boards for quality and scam risk
how: List the remote boards I use; ask Research to rate each on reputation, vetting, posting age and pay transparency, and suggest which to keep checking.

title: Build search recipes for sponsoring employers
how: Give my visa type and role; ask for search strings and filters that surface postings stating sponsorship, and a way to cross-check each employer against public filing data.

title: Navigate public-sector job portals and the keywords they use
how: Name my occupation; ask Research for the official portals, series or grade terms, the application format and timelines, and the keywords to put in my profile.

title: Find university and research staff job listings
how: Give my field; ask Claude where universities, labs and institutes post staff and research roles, search terms to use, and how those applications differ from corporate ones.

title: Search for internships and entry-level roles efficiently
how: Give my major and interests; ask for title strings, programs and filters for entry-level roles including those labeled as associate or trainee, and a weekly review checklist.

title: Prepare for a career fair with a ranked employer list
how: Paste the fair's employer list; ask Claude to rank 12 to visit, draft a question and a 30-second pitch for each, and plan the order and time to meet the most relevant.

title: Optimize my profile terms so recruiters find me
how: Give my profile and target roles; ask Claude for the search terms recruiters use for these roles, and where to place them in headline, skills and experience.

title: Write advanced search queries to find hidden profiles and pages
how: Give my target role and company types; ask for ten advanced search queries that find career pages, team pages and employee profiles using site and quoted phrases.

title: Deduplicate postings across boards into one list
how: Give Claude Code a folder of exported postings; ask for a script that matches duplicates by company and title and keeps one row with all links and posting dates.

title: Filter out stale postings before I spend time
how: Paste postings with dates; ask Claude to flag those older than three weeks or reposted, estimate stale-risk and sort remaining by recency and fit.

title: Sweep a list of company career pages in one session
how: Give Cowork my target company list; ask it to open each careers page, note open roles matching my filters, and return a sorted sheet with links and dates.

title: Collect and normalize apply links into my tracker
how: Give Cowork a tab list of postings; ask it to extract title, company, location, pay and apply link into a spreadsheet, flagging missing details.

title: Find hiring events and open days near me
how: Ask Research for hiring events, open days and sector fairs in my area in the next 30 days, tagging employers hiring my role and the registration deadlines.

title: Mine sector newsletters for hiring announcements
how: With the email connector, ask Claude to scan my newsletters for hires, funding and new product news, and list employers and people worth contacting this week.

title: Find apprenticeships and paid training that lead to jobs
how: Name my target field and region; ask Research for registered apprenticeships and paid training programs, eligibility, pay during training and placement rates where published.

title: Find returnship and re-entry programs
how: Ask Research for current returnship programs in my field, eligibility, cohort dates and application steps, and for employers that welcome candidates with career gaps.

title: Find contract and temp-to-hire routes into target employers
how: Name my target employers and role; ask Claude which agencies and contract programs feed them, how conversion usually works, and what to ask about it before accepting.

title: Find fractional and project-based leads in my specialty
how: Describe my specialty; ask for places and networks where fractional and project work is posted, the pitch for each, and a simple offer sheet of scope and rates.

title: Search postings using Spanish and English keywords
how: Give my role; ask for bilingual search strings including accent variants and regional terms, plus phrases like bilingual required, so I find roles posters list in either language.

title: Create location-flexible search variants
how: Give my target role and cities; ask for variant strings for remote, hybrid and relocation-friendly postings, and the phrases that hide remote options in location fields.

title: Search for postings above my pay floor
how: Give my pay floor; ask for search tactics that filter by pay, including boards with pay filters and phrases that show senior scope, and how to treat roles that do not post pay.

title: Create rules for apply, referral first or skip
how: Give my profile and preferences; ask Claude to write a rule set deciding whether to apply directly, seek a referral first or skip, based on fit score, posting age and network ties.

title: Automate a daily brief of top postings to my inbox
how: Ask Claude Code to build a small repo that runs daily, pulls feeds, scores postings against my criteria with rules, and emails me the top five with reasons.

title: Schedule recurring search blocks on my calendar
how: With the calendar connector, ask Claude to place daily 40-minute search blocks around my existing commitments, with a fixed agenda in each event description.

title: Prevent double applications to the same company
how: Give Claude my tracker and the email connector; ask it to check whether I already applied or heard from each new posting's employer and warn me before I apply twice.

title: Find community channels where jobs are shared
how: Name my field; ask Research for community chats, forums and mailing lists where members share jobs, their rules about self-promotion, and a way to introduce myself.

title: Use alumni and school job boards effectively
how: Describe my school; ask Claude how to find alumni boards and career-center resources, what to search, and how to contact alumni posters with a short opener.

title: Use professional association job boards and directories
how: Name my profession; ask Research for associations with job boards and member directories, their membership costs, events and chapters near me, and which have the best postings.

title: Build a list of local employers to approach directly
how: Name my role and area; ask Research for a table of 30 local employers that hire for it with the address, size and a contact path, ordered by proximity and fit.

title: Find government contractors hiring for my skills
how: Ask Research to find contractors holding recent public awards that need my skills, the teams, locations and whether clearances or registrations are required.

title: Find openings and moves inside my current employer
how: Paste my employer's internal posting titles or org notes I may share; ask Claude to suggest which teams fit my skills, who to talk to and how to ask about transfers without alarming my manager.

title: Turn one good posting into ten similar employers
how: Paste a posting I like; ask Research to find ten comparable employers with similar roles, and explain what each shares with the posting and where to find its openings.

title: Pitch a role that does not yet exist
how: Give a company problem I spotted and my skills; ask Claude to draft a short proposal email and one-page outline showing the problem, my approach, and a low-risk first project.

title: Filter remote postings by time zone and legal constraints
how: Give my time zone and country; ask Claude to read each posting for overlap-hour requirements and country restrictions, and mark which I can actually accept.

title: Scan postings for hidden language requirements
how: Paste postings; ask Claude to identify stated and implied language requirements, level, written versus spoken, and flag which roles reward my bilingual skills.

title: Pick and approach three staffing agencies well
how: Give my field and region and the list of agencies Research returns; ask Claude to rank three, draft a short note for each recruiter and a checklist of questions to ask before signing anything.

title: Review the week's discovery results and tune searches
how: Paste a week of search results with notes; ask Claude to say which searches produced the best postings, which to drop or rephrase, and a new search to try.

title: Search by skills and tasks instead of job titles
how: Give my main tasks and tools; ask for search phrases that use duties and skills to surface postings with unfamiliar titles, and a list of titles that appear most for those tasks.

title: Find employers via grants, awards and public registries
how: Name my field; ask Research to find recent grant recipients, award winners and registered organizations in my area, and to rank by size and likelihood to be hiring.

title: Tailor my resume to one posting without inventing anything
how: Paste the posting and my master resume; ask Claude to reorder and reword to mirror the posting's language, change nothing factual, and list every edit so I can approve it.

title: Build a long master resume to cut tailored versions from
how: Put all roles, projects and metrics in a Project; ask Claude to assemble a complete master document with 8 to 12 bullets per role, which I trim per application.

title: Rewrite weak bullets as accomplishment, measure and method
how: Paste ten duty-style bullets with facts about results; ask for rewrites that start with a strong verb, state a measurable outcome and the method, and flag where numbers are missing.

title: Check keyword coverage against a posting
how: Paste posting and resume; ask Claude to list the posting's key terms, mark which appear in my resume, and suggest truthful places to add the missing ones in natural sentences.

title: Make my resume format survive applicant-tracking parsing
how: Paste my resume text and describe its layout; ask Claude to point out tables, columns, icons and headers that parsers mishandle, and give a plain single-column version.

title: Cut my resume to one page without losing the strongest evidence
how: Paste my resume; ask Claude to cut to one page, ranking bullets by relevance to a named target role, and show what was removed so I can veto.

title: Structure a two-page resume for a senior career
how: Paste my full history; ask for a two-page layout with a summary of scope, selected achievements, compressed early roles and board or advisory items last, with word budgets per section.

title: Write a summary that states target, proof and scope
how: Give my target role, years and three top results; ask for three summary options of 3 lines each with no clichés, and note which fits applicant-tracking and human readers best.

title: Design a skills section organized for scanning
how: List my skills and tools and a target posting; ask Claude to group and order them for relevance, drop filler such as generic soft skills, and mark proficiency honestly.

title: Restructure a resume for a career change
how: Paste my resume and target posting; ask for a functional-hybrid structure with a relevant-experience section up top, translated terms, and a short note on reducing the old title's weight.

title: Draft a first resume from coursework and projects
how: Give my education, classes, projects, jobs and activities; ask Claude to build a one-page resume with project bullets showing problem, action and result, and flag what to leave off.

title: Decide where to place education and honors
how: Give my degree, GPA and honors and target role; ask Claude whether education goes first, whether to list GPA, and how to phrase relevant coursework without padding.

title: Create a bilingual resume pair in English and Spanish
how: Paste my English resume; ask for a natural Spanish version using local conventions (such as a photo or personal data norms for the country, which I will verify) and consistent titles in both.

title: Adapt a resume to Latin American CV conventions
how: Name the country; ask Research for the local CV expectations on length, photo, personal data and references, then ask Claude to apply them to my resume and mark items I should confirm.

title: Translate my resume while keeping titles and claims accurate
how: Paste my resume and the target language; ask for a faithful translation with local equivalents of titles, a glossary of terms, and notes on any phrase that might mislead.

title: Choose resume or CV format for the target country
how: Name the country and role type; ask Claude whether a resume, CV or Europass-style document is expected there, and how to reformat mine.

title: Emphasize remote-work evidence on my resume
how: Paste my resume; ask Claude to surface async communication, tools, time-zone coordination and self-management evidence in bullets, and add a short remote work line to the summary.

title: Show licenses and compliance record correctly
how: List my licenses, audits and regulatory experience; ask Claude to place them where reviewers expect, state identifiers appropriately and rewrite bullets with the standards and outcomes.

title: Build a sales resume around quota and pipeline numbers
how: Give quota, attainment, deal sizes and cycle times by year; ask Claude to produce bullets that lead with attainment percentages and ranks, and a header line of career totals.

title: Shape a resume for consulting screens
how: Paste my resume; ask for bullets framed as problem, structured approach and quantified impact, with leadership and analytical evidence in the order consulting screeners look for.

title: Shape a resume for product and project roles
how: Paste my resume; ask Claude to recast work as outcomes driven (users, revenue, delivery time), show cross-functional scope and decision-making, and keep tool lists short.

title: Show retention and satisfaction evidence for customer roles
how: Give retention, satisfaction, resolution time and account figures; ask Claude to write bullets that show relationships and results, and a summary stating the customer segments I served.

title: Quantify operations achievements for the resume
how: Give throughput, cost, error and lead-time numbers before and after my changes; ask Claude for bullets that show scale, savings and method such as process change or tooling.

title: Rewrite engineering resume bullets around impact and scope
how: Paste bullets and project facts; ask for rewrites that state the system, scale, my specific contribution and outcome, and cut buzzword lists and unproven technology claims.

title: Show people leadership with numbers on the resume
how: Give team sizes, promotions, retention and goals met; ask Claude for bullets that show hiring, coaching and delivery outcomes, and a leadership summary line.

title: Present AI and automation work as business results
how: Describe automations and AI workflows I built with their time saved and users; ask Claude for bullets stating the problem, tool choices and measured results without hype, plus honest limits.

title: Write the resume line that handles a layoff without apology
how: Describe the layoff circumstances; ask Claude for one neutral factual line on the resume or cover letter and a 20-second spoken version, with no over-explaining.

title: Present employment gaps clearly on the resume
how: Give my dates and what I did in the gaps; ask Claude to choose between year-only dates, a short gap line, or showing relevant activities, and to explain the trade-offs.

title: Frame short stints so they read as deliberate
how: Paste my history with reasons for each short stay; ask Claude to group contract and project roles, state reasons succinctly, and highlight results delivered in the time.

title: Show promotions and scope growth within one employer
how: Paste my titles and dates at one employer; ask for a layout showing each title with its own bullets or a stacked format, that parsers read correctly.

title: Extract the keyword set from ten similar postings
how: Paste ten postings for my target role; ask Claude to produce a ranked keyword and phrase list and a template resume section that works across most of them.

title: Remove repeated verbs and filler phrases
how: Paste the resume; ask Claude to find repeated opening verbs, phrases like responsible for, and passive voice, and rewrite them with specific alternatives without changing meaning.

title: Audit every claim on the resume for defensibility
how: Paste the resume; ask Claude to question each claim as an interviewer would, mark those where I need numbers, a source or a story, and flag anything that could look inflated.

title: Test whether the resume reads in a 15-second skim
how: Paste the resume and the posting; ask Claude to summarize what a recruiter would remember after 15 seconds, what they miss, and the three changes that most improve that skim.

title: Make two versions of the resume and track which works
how: Ask Claude to produce two variants differing in one element (summary or top bullet set), a naming scheme, and a tracker column so I can compare reply rates after 20 applications.

title: Clean file name, metadata and format before sending
how: Ask Claude for a checklist and file-naming convention for each submission, including PDF versus docx rules, removing hidden metadata and checking links and phone number.

title: Build a resume from my exported profile data
how: Paste my exported profile sections; ask Claude to turn them into a focused resume with a chosen length and target, noting what the profile contains that the resume should omit.

title: Draft resume bullets from my repository history
how: Point Claude Code at my repos and commit logs; ask it to propose bullets with what I built, size and measurable outcomes, citing the commits as evidence, and flag anything unverifiable.

title: Generate a clean resume from a template in a repo
how: Ask Claude Code to set up a repo with a data file and a template that builds a resume PDF in two variants, so tailoring means editing data and running one command.

title: Keep resume versions per application in a repo
how: Ask Claude Code to create a folder per application with the posting, the tailored resume and a diff against the master, so I can see what I claimed to whom.

title: Automate first-draft tailoring for each saved posting
how: Ask Claude Code to build a script that takes a posting file and my master data, produces a tailored resume draft and a change list, that I review before sending.

title: Brief a human reviewer so their feedback is useful
how: Ask Claude to write a short message and checklist for a friend or mentor to review my resume, with three specific questions, so I receive actionable comments.

title: Create a short career fair handout version
how: Give my resume and the target employers; ask for a one-page version and a 30-second spoken companion with two variants for different employer types.

title: Prepare a long-form resume for formal government applications
how: Give my history and the announcement text; ask Claude to build a detailed resume mirroring the announcement's duty and qualification language, with hours per week and supervisors, which I will verify.

title: Convert an academic CV into a two-page industry resume
how: Paste the CV; ask Claude to cut publications to the few that matter, translate research into industry outcomes, and add a skills block built from target postings.

title: Place portfolio and profile links where reviewers click
how: Ask Claude to suggest link placement, short labels and a QR-free format, and check that each link goes to a page that supports a claim on the resume.

title: Find every bullet missing a number or outcome
how: Paste the resume; ask Claude to mark bullets without a result and ask me one question each so I can supply scale, frequency or outcome, then rewrite with the figures labeled as estimates where needed.

title: Tune the density so the page is readable
how: Paste the resume; ask for suggestions on margins, spacing, bullets per role and sentences to trim, aiming at readable rather than packed, and give a before and after word count.

title: Prune old experience that no longer helps
how: Paste my full history; ask Claude to decide which roles to compress to a line, which to drop, and how to keep a complete history when forms require it.

title: Check that my resume is findable in recruiter database searches
how: Paste my resume and three target titles; ask Claude to judge whether the exact titles and skills a recruiter would search appear, and where to add them honestly.

title: Write a promotion case document from my record
how: Paste my goals, results and feedback; ask Claude to draft a one-page promotion case with impact against the next level's expectations and the evidence for each, to review with my manager.

title: Proofread the final resume for typos and consistency
how: Paste the final text; ask Claude to check spelling, tense, date formats, punctuation consistency and numbers, and read it back aloud style so errors that spell-check misses stand out.

title: Set honesty rules so tailoring never becomes fabrication
how: Add instructions to a Project telling Claude to use only facts from my records, mark invented-looking claims, and ask me before adding any skill I did not list, then reuse it for every edit.

title: Create one resume per role family from the master
how: With my master in a Project, ask Claude for three role-family versions (such as analyst, operations and project), each with a distinct summary and bullet order, and a rule for choosing among them.

title: Draft a targeted cover letter in under 250 words
how: Paste the posting, my resume and one fact about the employer; ask for a 200-word letter with an opening that states my fit, two proof points and a clear close, in my voice samples.

title: Write five distinct opening lines for a cover letter
how: Give the posting and my best result; ask for five openings (result-first, problem-first, referral-first, mission-first, direct) that avoid I am writing to apply, and say which suits this employer.

title: Teach Claude my writing voice from my own samples
how: Add three of my emails or posts to a Project; ask Claude to describe my voice rules and then use them in letters so drafts sound like me and not like a template.

title: Decide whether a cover letter helps for this application
