how: Give the posting and my resume; ask for a three-part pack: a 3-line blurb about me, the three reasons I fit and the resume file, written so the referrer can paste it into the referral form in 2 minutes.

title: Map who in my network touches each target employer
how: Paste my contact list or exported connections and my target employers; ask Claude to match people to employers, rank by closeness and write down the first move for each.

title: Analyze my exported contacts for hidden ties
how: Give Claude Code my exported contacts file; ask for a script that groups people by employer, industry and city, finds second-degree paths to target companies and outputs a ranked outreach list.

title: Ask a mutual contact for a warm introduction
how: Give the person I want to meet, our mutual contact and the reason; ask for a forwardable request with a 50-word blurb about me and an easy opt-out, so the mutual contact only has to paste it.

title: Request an informational interview with a 15-minute ask
how: Give the person's role and one specific thing I admire in their work; ask for a 70-word request stating my goal, a 15-minute limit and two time slots, with no job request.

title: Prepare questions for an informational interview
how: Give the person's profile and my goal; ask for 10 questions ordered from background to advice, with three that only they can answer, and a closing question asking who else to talk to.

title: Turn call notes into a summary and next actions
how: Paste my rough notes; ask Claude to summarize insights, vocabulary to learn, names to follow up with and two specific actions, and draft a thank-you that references one detail.

title: Send a thank-you that keeps the door open
how: Give notes from the call and the advice I will follow; ask for a 60-word note naming one piece of advice I will act on, and a date when I will update them on the result.

title: Ask the person I interviewed for two further introductions
how: Give the call context; ask Claude to write a closing request for two names that sounds natural, with a forwardable blurb so they can introduce me quickly.

title: Write an event networking script with openers and exits
how: Give the event, who will attend and my goals; ask for three openers, five follow-up questions, a graceful exit line, and a target of three real conversations.

title: Research the attendees and speakers before an event
how: Give the attendee list or speaker page; ask Research to pick the five people most relevant to my goal, one thing to ask each and a reason they might want to speak with me.

title: Send follow-ups in the 48 hours after an event
how: Paste my notes on whom I met; ask Claude for individualized messages that mention something said, give value such as an article, and propose the next step, ready to send within two days.

title: Plan engagement with alumni groups and chapters
how: Give my school and city; ask for a plan using alumni directories, chapters and mentoring programs, with a message template and a weekly goal of three alumni conversations.

title: Use career center and mentor programs fully
how: Describe what my school offers; ask Claude to list each service, how to prepare for it, and how to turn a mentor program match into a referral chain over three meetings.

title: Use association events and chapters to meet hiring managers
how: Name my association; ask Claude for a plan to volunteer for a committee or event, which roles bring contact with managers, and a message to the chapter lead.

title: Contact an employee at a target employer with no connection
how: Give the person's role, a public detail and my goal; ask for a 70-word message of a specific question about the work and a request for a 10-minute chat, and avoid asking for a job.

title: Revive dormant contacts without a hard ask
how: Give a list of old contacts with the last topic; ask for short reconnection notes referencing that topic and one update from me, sent a few a week, asking how they are before any request.

title: Ask a senior person to sponsor my move
how: Describe the person and my goal; ask Claude for a message asking for advice on a specific decision, then a second message after the call proposing how they might help.

title: Plan internal conversations for a transfer
how: List the teams I am interested in; ask for a plan of three conversations with questions, a script to ask for coffee and the way to signal interest to my manager at the right time.

title: Build a written-first networking plan
how: Describe my comfort level; ask Claude to design a plan based on thoughtful written messages, comments and small group chats, with a path from message to a short call.

title: Plan networking in two hours a week
how: Give my two-hour budget; ask for a weekly schedule: 3 messages, 1 follow-up, 1 call, with templates and a tracker so none are forgotten.

title: Find Spanish and bilingual professional communities
how: Name my field and location; ask Research for professional groups, chambers and associations that serve Spanish speakers, their events and how to join and contribute.

title: Build a network in a Latin American market from abroad
how: Name country and field; ask Research for associations, expat groups, alumni chapters and events, then ask Claude for an outreach message in Spanish and a 90-day plan.

title: Use diaspora and alumni links to reach employers
how: Describe my background and target country; ask Claude to propose groups and alumni lists of people who moved or returned, and write a message that refers to our shared roots.

title: Build relationships in remote-first communities
how: Name the communities I joined; ask Claude for a plan of helpful contributions, questions to ask and a way to move from public threads to a private conversation.

title: Talk with employees who were sponsored at target employers
how: Give public profiles of employees who moved from my country; ask Claude for a short message asking about their path, the team's sponsorship practice and what they would do again.

title: Activate my network after a layoff with specific asks
how: Give my target role and a list of contacts; ask for a short announcement message and individual asks (intros to named roles), emphasizing what I do and not the layoff.

title: Organize a mutual job lead exchange with laid-off peers
how: Ask Claude to draft an invitation and a simple weekly agenda for a small group sharing leads, introductions and practice interviews, with rules to keep it useful and confidential.

title: Write a networking script for someone entering a new field
how: Give my story and target field; ask for an opener that states my background, the move and a precise question, and three follow-ups that show I did my homework.

title: Ask senior peers about unposted roles
how: Give my profile and the kind of role; ask for a short message to peers and former bosses describing the exact role I want, why now and how they could help, without asking for a favor.

title: Use board members, investors and advisors as paths in
how: Give the target and public information on its investors and advisors; ask Claude to propose a route to each, and write a concise note to the most promising connection.

title: Build durable relationships with recruiters
how: Give the recruiters I have met; ask for a quarterly update message that shares my progress, tells them what I want next and offers a referral or name in return.

title: Find ways to offer value to contacts before asking
how: List my contacts and what I know about their goals; ask Claude to suggest a useful article, introduction or small favor for each, to send without any request.

title: Update referrers on outcomes to keep them in my corner
how: Describe the result and what the referrer did; ask for a short message that thanks them for the specific action, shares the outcome and offers help in return.

title: Plan the follow-up cadence after a referral
how: Give the referral date and process; ask Claude for a schedule of when to check with the referrer, the recruiter and the hiring manager, and the message for each.

title: Set up a personal contact tracker with reminders
how: With the calendar connector, ask Claude to set recurring reminders and a simple tracker format that records each person, last contact, next step and notes, so no warm lead goes cold.

title: Find forgotten contacts and threads in my inbox
how: With the email connector, ask Claude to search my mail for past colleagues, clients and recruiters who work at my target employers, and list people to reconnect with and when we last spoke.

title: Schedule networking calls without back-and-forth
how: With the calendar connector, ask Claude to propose three time slots that fit my calendar, write the reply with them, and add confirmed calls with a prep note in the event.

title: Prepare a one-page brief before each networking call
how: With the calendar connector, ask Claude to read tomorrow's call events and write a brief for each: who they are, our shared points, three questions and my ask.

title: Practice a coffee chat with Claude playing the contact
how: Give the contact's profile; ask Claude to play them in a 10-minute conversation, challenge vague answers, then critique my opening, curiosity and closing.

title: Use volunteering and boards to meet decision makers
how: Describe my interests; ask Claude for volunteer roles and community boards where hiring managers show up and an introduction that offers a skill, not a job request.

title: Pitch myself for a small talk or panel
how: Give my expertise and a target event; ask Claude to write a speaker pitch with title, three takeaways and a bio, since talks bring inbound contacts.

title: Use public posts as a reason to start a conversation
how: Paste a post by someone I want to reach; ask Claude for a reply that adds a specific idea and a follow-up message that moves it to a conversation, within two days.

title: Choose three local meetups and plan how to use them
how: Ask Research for recurring meetups in my area in my field; ask Claude to rank three and give me an arrival, conversation and follow-up plan for the first visit.

title: Find a mentor with a specific, small ask
how: Describe what I want to learn; ask Claude to help pick candidates, write a request for one question and one meeting, then a follow-up that builds toward a longer relationship.

title: Start a peer mentoring circle for job seekers
how: Ask Claude to design a six-person circle: invitation, ground rules, a meeting agenda and exercises such as mock interviews and referral exchanges.

title: Turn a campus or recruiting event into an interview
how: Give the employer rep's name and what we discussed; ask for a short email within 24 hours reminding them of the conversation, attaching my resume and asking about the next stage.

title: Plan a four-step ladder from connection to a call
how: Give the person and my reason; ask for four messages spaced over three weeks: connect, share something useful, ask a question, request a call, with an exit if no reply.

title: Score contacts by usefulness and warmth
how: Paste a list of contacts; ask for an Artifact that scores each by closeness, access to my targets and recent contact, and sorts the top 20 to approach first.

title: Write a cold email to a hiring manager about an open role
how: Give the manager's role, the posting and one relevant result of mine; ask for a 90-word email with a subject line, a specific reason I fit and a request for a short call.

title: Write a cold email to a manager for a role that is not posted
how: Give the manager's public work and my best proof; ask for a 100-word email describing a problem I can help with, a small example and a request to talk.

title: Write an intro message to a recruiter at a target firm
how: Give the recruiter's name and openings; ask for a 70-word note with my target role, location, key proof and availability, and a clear question about fit.

title: Reply to an inbound recruiter message to keep options open
how: Paste the recruiter message; ask for a reply that asks for pay range, remote policy and team, states my interests, and protects confidentiality.

title: List questions to ask a recruiter before agreeing to a process
how: Paste the role summary; ask for eight questions on pay range, stages, timeline, team, reasons for the opening and visa policy, so I can decide whether to spend time.

title: Write a follow-up after applying with no reply
how: Give the application date, role and any contact; ask for a 60-word follow-up for a recruiter or hiring manager that restates my fit and asks about timeline, to send after one week.

title: Plan three follow-ups over four weeks
how: Give my contacts and the application history; ask for three short messages with different content (new proof, relevant news, polite close) and exact send dates.

title: Write a follow-up that adds value after an interview
how: Give the interview notes and one question I handled weakly; ask for a 120-word note that thanks the person for a specific moment, adds the missing point and restates my interest.

title: Follow up after silence post final round
how: Give the dates and the last message; ask for two versions: a light check and a decision-timeline ask, and advise on when to stop.

title: Generate subject lines and test which gets replies
how: Give my message and audience; ask for ten subject lines under 50 characters in different styles, avoid spammy words, and recommend which two to test with a note-taking method.

title: Personalize outreach to 20 people with a research table
how: Give a table of 20 contacts with one public fact each and my core message; ask Claude to write 20 individually personalized messages of under 90 words, marking weak personalization for me to fix.

title: Create outreach as drafts in my email, never sent automatically
how: With the email connector, ask Claude to place each personalized message in my drafts with the recipient and subject, so I review and send manually.

title: Track replies and flag who needs a follow-up
how: With the email connector, ask Claude each week to scan sent outreach and replies, list threads with no answer after 7 days, and propose which to follow up and which to drop.

title: Create follow-up reminders on my calendar
how: With the calendar connector, ask Claude to add follow-up events for each outreach at 5 and 12 days, with the draft text in the description, so nothing falls through.

title: Reply to scheduling and logistics messages quickly
how: With the email and calendar connectors, ask Claude to draft replies offering available slots for interview and call requests, and put holds on my calendar once confirmed.

title: Write outreach in natural Spanish for regional contacts
how: Give the contact, country and my goal; ask for a Spanish message with correct formality for that country, polite openers and a specific request, and an English version for my records.

title: Write a note to a recruiter who needs bilingual talent
how: Give the posting; ask for a short message in the posting's language stating my level in each language with a work example and availability, offering a short call in either.

title: Pitch a US remote employer on hiring from Latin America
how: Give my country, time zone and the company's posting; ask for a message that covers overlap hours, contract options and why my regional knowledge helps, in a confident and short form.

title: Ask about sponsorship early without hurting my chances
how: Give the role and my status; ask for a neutral wording to ask the recruiter about sponsorship in the first contact, and a response if they say they do not sponsor.

title: Write outreach that leads with transferable results
how: Give my background and the target role; ask for a message that states the move once, gives two relevant results and requests a brief conversation about how to prove readiness.

title: Write outreach for students asking about internships
how: Give my major and the team; ask for a 70-word message that mentions a relevant class or project, asks about the team's internship process and offers to send my resume.

title: Write outreach from a senior candidate to peers and executives
how: Give the executive's priorities and my record; ask for a short message framing a shared problem, offering one relevant insight and proposing a brief conversation, in an understated tone.

title: Write the first message to recruiters after a layoff
how: Give my target role and availability; ask for a short message to recruiters stating that I am available now, my top proof, and what I seek, with no apology.

title: Write discreet outreach while employed
how: Give my situation; ask for messages that mention confidentiality, ask recruiters to keep the discussion private, and avoid using my work email or time.

title: Write a 20-second voicemail or call script
how: Give the contact and my reason; ask Claude for a 20-second script with a clear name, reason and callback, plus a text message variant.

title: Write a close-the-loop message after a rejection
how: Paste the rejection; ask for a gracious reply that thanks them, asks to stay in touch, and requests feedback in one question, without pressing.

title: Ask for feedback after a rejection in a way that gets answers
how: Paste the rejection and my interview notes; ask for a 50-word message with one specific question, such as what the strongest candidate showed, which is easy to answer in a sentence.

title: Re-engage a company three months after a rejection
how: Give what has changed since the process; ask for a short message to the recruiter sharing a relevant new result and asking about openings, with a calendar reminder.

title: Decline or pause a process while keeping goodwill
how: Describe my reason; ask for a short professional message that declines or reschedules and leaves the door open, with wording for a recruiter and for a manager.

title: Tell a recruiter I have another offer to speed a process
how: Give my timeline and the other offer's deadline; ask for a truthful message that asks about their timeline, states a competing deadline neutrally and keeps goodwill.

title: Write a message under 300 characters that gets answered
how: Give the person's role and my ask; ask for four short-form messages of under 300 characters with one idea each, a question at the end and no attachments.

title: Create a playbook for each type of reply
how: Ask Claude to build a Project with response templates for yes, maybe later, not hiring, referral to someone else, and ignored, so I answer each in two minutes.

title: Prepare answers for the common brush-offs
how: List the replies I get (no budget, send your resume online, not hiring); ask Claude to write one short, polite, specific answer for each that moves toward a conversation.

title: Calibrate tone for different industries and levels
how: Give three sample messages and the audiences; ask Claude to rewrite each in the register that suits finance, a startup and a nonprofit, and mark what changed.

title: Track what messages get replies
how: Ask for an Artifact tracker with columns for message version, audience, date and reply, that computes the reply rate by version and tells me when the sample is too small to decide.

title: Check messages against anti-spam and platform rules
how: Paste my message template and volume; ask Claude to check for spammy patterns, limits and etiquette on email and professional networks, and suggest safer pacing.

title: Send a short value note with an idea for their team
how: Give public details of the team's work and my idea; ask for a 120-word note with a specific, small suggestion and evidence it works, ending with a question and no job ask.

title: Send a periodic update to warm contacts
how: Give my recent projects and progress; ask for a short monthly update message with one result, one request for introductions, and a clear role I want, to send to 30 contacts.

title: Write a note to a startup founder about joining early
how: Give the product and my relevant results; ask for an 80-word note that names a problem I can solve in 30 days, and offers a small trial task.

title: Pitch a local business owner on a role
how: Give the business and my skills; ask Claude for a short message or in-person script showing I know what they sell, describing a problem I can address, and asking for a brief meeting.

title: Write a contract-focused note to staffing recruiters
how: Give my skills, rates and start date; ask for a note that lists availability, rate range, clearances or credentials and the contract types I accept.

title: Ask someone to be my reference with the right context
how: Give the role, the person and our shared projects; ask for a message that states the role, three points I hope they can speak to and the deadline, with a brief and an easy exit.

title: Prepare a briefing sheet for my references
how: Give the posting and the reference's history with me; ask for a one-page sheet with the role, my strengths, projects they saw and likely questions, to send before the call.

title: Plan a weekly outreach batch of 15 messages
how: Give my target list and my time; ask Claude to pick 15 contacts, write the messages, set send days and schedule follow-ups, finishing in a single 90-minute session.

title: Write outreach that explains a career break in one line
how: Give the circumstances; ask for message wording that states the break plainly in one clause and moves quickly to my relevant work and current goal.

title: Write a message to a group of interviewers at once
how: Give the names and roles on the panel; ask for a thank-you that references each person briefly, with a single group email and a separate short note to the lead.

title: Ask a former manager for leads and a reference at once
how: Give my history with the manager and my target role; ask for a short message that updates them, asks who they know hiring and whether they would be a reference, with an easy no.

title: Contact in-house talent teams directly
how: Give the employer and the posting; ask for a message to the in-house recruiter that names the role ID, my two most relevant facts and a request to confirm my application is seen.

title: Ask for the pay range early without awkwardness
how: Give the posting and the recruiter's name; ask for two wordings asking for the pay range before investing time, one email and one for the first call.

title: Reopen a thread that went quiet in the process
how: Paste the last messages; ask for a short, friendly message that adds new information and a single easy question, and one that closes the loop if I need to move on.

title: Reach out to a team after a reorganization
how: Give news of the reorganization and my skills; ask for a message that acknowledges the change, shows how I could help with the new priorities and requests a short call.
